name: an-idle-page-leaves-no-orphan-surfaces
description: Five idle minutes with a page open must log zero "Old/orphaned temporary reference" lines. Viz writes that line (surface_manager.cc, ExpireOldTemporaryReferences) when a frame sink submits a surface with a new LocalSurfaceId and no embedder ever references it within 10 to 20 seconds - the surface leaks a temporary reference and viz drops it. WHAT THIS GUARDS: Atrium's own surfaces. The sidebar, the command bar, the pill, the devbar, the AI panel and the tab pane are all top-level WebContents in views::Widgets Atrium owns, and every one of them has to end up embedded in a compositor that actually draws. A change that leaves one attached to a widget that never draws, or that resizes a surface behind a hidden widget, starts printing this line and this scenario turns red. WHAT IT DOES NOT GUARD: page content. A cross-origin iframe the page itself keeps re-laying-out while its embedder never paints it produces the same line, and that is upstream Chromium behaviour on real web content, not something Atrium decides - measured 2026-09-05: a fixture with cross-site iframes under transform/content-visibility that hides them from paint printed 62 of these lines in 75 seconds, while the whole existing scenario corpus (1055 recorded runs, 73 million run-log lines) printed none. So the fixture here is deliberately a plain single-origin page with no iframes: the only frame sinks in the run are the ones Atrium put there. The line is a DLOG, so it exists only because the dev build sets DCHECK_ALWAYS_ON. An official build compiles it out and this scenario would prove nothing against one.

actions.note: let the startup space's tab commit

GATE: a page really committed. Without it a launch that never reached a page would idle for five minutes and pass on an empty log, which is the one way a vlog_absent assertion goes green while measuring nothing. Either host counts - two-tabs.spaces.json carries both and lastActiveAt, not file order, picks the starting one.
Five idle minutes, the window the task asks for. The expiry timer runs every 10 seconds and needs a reference to survive two ticks, so this covers about 30 chances to print the line.

assertions.label: no-orphan-surface
assertions.desc: THE ASSERTION. Listed before quit on purpose: the run log is pulled once before assertions run, so this reads the idle period and not the teardown. Shutdown destroys every surface widget at once and a temporary reference outstanding at that moment is a different, uninteresting thing.
the app was still alive and showing its window for those five minutes, so the clean log above is a statement about a running browser rather than a dead one
and it was still responsive enough to quit on Cmd+Q
